topic: Surveillance backlash and AI social license
angle: AI deployment fails when you win the contract but lose the community.
sourceTitle: Flock is tightening its rules in response to a growing surveillance backlash
linkedinPost:
Winning the RFP isn’t the same as earning permission to operate.

MIT Technology Review reports a police-tech vendor is tightening access to its license-plate reader network after backlash and lost contracts. The pattern is familiar: launch fast, scale faster, then scramble when the social license collapses.

Enterprises hit similar walls with AI that touches customers or citizens. The failure modes rhyme:
- Ambiguous use policies no one enforces.
- Vague opt-outs buried in settings.
- Thin audit trails you can’t defend in public.

My take from deployments: Treat social license as a product requirement. Write “abuse stories” alongside user stories. Ship with clear consent flows, visible controls, and third-party audit hooks. Stand up an internal red team to pressure-test misuse before the press does.

If your AI changes people’s rights, choices, or safety, you need more than compliance. You need legitimacy, measured in renewals and absence of headlines.

What’s one safeguard you’d add if you assumed your worst critic would read your logs tomorrow? #AIStrategy #AITransformation #EnterpriseAI
